title: Sequence-aware SLO Orchestrator + KV-prefetch Heatmap and Failback Dashboard
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Objective: Build instrumentation and a dashboard surface that ties token-level latency SLIs (sequence-aware) to KV-prefetch behavior and multi-region failback decisions. Deliver a runbook and rollout plan so on-call can interpret heatmap signals and trigger containment actions (circuit hysteresis adjustments, shed rules).

Background: We currently have per-token p95/p99 telemetry and region-level SLO orchestration work (see ENG-412992, ENG-331442). However, gaps remain in correlating sequence-level latency spikes with KV-prefetch misses, admission/eviction events, and cross-region spillover. This ticket creates a composite dashboard and a short runbook for failback/circuit decisioning plus the SLO orchestrator hooks to automate initial mitigation (admit-hysteresis bump, targeted route fallback).
acceptance_criteria: A composite dashboard in Grafana that shows: token p50/p95/p99 over time, per-sequence latency waterfall, KV-prefetch hit/miss heatmap (grouped by model shard and region), admission queue depth, and circuit-breaker state timelines
New metric: sequence_latency_ms_by_token exported with sequence_id and token_index tags, aggregated at 5s and 1m rollups
KV-prefetch metrics: kv_prefetch_requests, kv_prefetch_hits, kv_prefetch_miss_penalty_ms; heatmap panel supports pivot by region and shard
Runbook created and published with steps to interpret heatmap and to perform manual rollback or temporary admit-hysteresis increase
Orchestrator hook implemented: when composite SLO error budget burn > 30% in 10m AND kv_prefetch_miss_rate>0.15, trigger targeted route fallback to lower-memory quantized variant
Unit/integration test coverage for new metrics exporters and a synthetic traffic scenario that reproduces the observed spike pattern
Documentation link in Console runbooks and PagerDuty escalation notes updated
updates: 2026-02-18 - Ticket created by Liam O'Connor. Initial scoping meeting scheduled with Observability and Runtime teams.

2026-02-22 - Spike completed: prototyped sequence_latency_ms_by_token using eBPF-derived timing in the serving runtime. Found 12-18% additional overhead for 1ms sampling; added guard to enable only for synthetic traffic by default. Notes: see Google Drive doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/seq-latency-spike-prototype

2026-02-28 - Design review with Observability (Nina Patel) and Runtime (Hassan Mir) - agreed to roll metric at 5s and 1m cardinality; avoid high-cardinality labels on production by hashing sequence_id to seq_hash with 256 bins.

2026-03-02 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2197 - exporters: add sequence_latency_ms_by_token and kv_prefetch_miss_penalty_ms. Runtime unit tests added. Requesting review from infra-metrics team.

2026-03-05 - Implemented Grafana dashboard skeleton: panels for token-level histograms, KV-prefetch heatmap pivotable by shard/region, circuit state timeline. Dashboard JSON in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/dashboards/seq-kv-heatmap.json

2026-03-08 - Observability feedback: heatmap needs logarithmic color scale to highlight low-volume but high-penalty misses; admission queue chart should correlate by request priority. Updated panels and noted follow-up UX tuning.

2026-03-10 - Orchestrator hook prototype added in orchestrator service: rule evaluation and dry-run logging established. Manual tests run in staging to simulate region spillover with synthetic workload. Next: finalize runbook and schedule on-call walkthrough.

Planned - 2026-03-12 to 2026-03-18: finalize PR reviews, merge exporters, enable metric sampling in staged routes, and run 48h stability test with synthetic traffic. Publish runbook prior to merge candidate.
Planned - 2026-03-20: rollout to canary with auto-roll back if error budget burn > 50% in 15m during canary window
notes: Design trade-offs: chose seq_hash bucketing to avoid high-cardinality sequence_id label in metrics; loses ability to surface single-sequence outliers but preserves production metric cardinality budgets.

Risk: exporting token-level histograms at high frequency can increase ingestion costs. Mitigation: sample only for trajectories where admission_queue_depth>5 OR for synthetic-only sampling by default. A follow-up ticket will explore prefix caching telemetry instead of token-level for long sequences.

On-call considerations: provide a short-play runbook snippet for engineers to triage whether spike is caused by prefetch storm vs kernel scheduling vs network spikes. Include recommended temporary knobs: increase admit-hysteresis by 20% for affected shard, enable route fallback, and pause autoscale expansion to avoid compounding latency.

Follow-ups: a) product ask to add a Console SLO view that surfaces sequence-aware burn; b) add automated annotation to timeline when orchestrator triggers fallback so root-cause analysis links to mitigation events
